description: Server-side request forgery: the caller choosing which machine the application talks to from inside the network. The second route passes untrusted data into a URL whose host is already fixed by a literal, leaving only a path segment, and is not a finding. The third sends caller data to a fixed destination, which is a different judgement about a different argument of the same call. The stated cost of that discriminator is a false negative on `"https://" + host`, which is composed and genuinely caller-chosen; that shape is rarer than a fixed base with a variable path, and a miss is the cheaper error than flooding every service that builds a URL from an id. The last pair is about position. A composed destination is normally not this judgement -- a fixed host with a caller-chosen path segment cannot be moved to another machine -- but when the caller's value comes FIRST the program wrote nothing in front of it. Asking instead whether a literal at the call names a scheme was tried and measured, and it readmitted two production call sites that keep their base URL in a constant.

expected.note: the whole destination comes from the caller; resolves fully now that a default import is qualified by its module
a composition, and the difference from the fixed-host one above is POSITION: the caller's value comes first, so nothing precedes it and the program named no destination at all
